A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SepLLM research. Their complete text, tables, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original training-free evaluations, training experiments, streaming measurements, ablations and retrieval results.

after.justification: v6 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons and separator-related experiments in Tables 9 and 15–17.

M1.justification: SepLLM's fundamental and streaming procedures remain unchanged. v6 introduces FixLLM as a diagnostic variant that replaces separator-based retention outside the initial and neighboring windows with fixed-interval token selection (Section 4.7, Appendix I).

E1.justification: Training datasets, downstream tasks, streaming benchmarks and Needle-in-a-Haystack coverage are retained. The new comparisons and controls reuse GSM8K-CoT and MMLU without introducing new data domains or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Beyond v4's full-attention and StreamingLLM comparisons, v6 evaluates H2O, SnapKV and PyramidKV on GSM8K-CoT (Table 15), a mixed sliding-window/full-attention-head baseline on MMLU (Table 9), and FixLLM on both benchmarks (Table 17). This substantially broadens evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce approximately matched runtime-KV budgets, head-fraction/window configurations, separator subsets and FixLLM intervals of four or five tokens. Existing few-shot settings, metrics, backbones and training budgets remain unchanged; the additions do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: Tables 9, 16 and 17 add targeted tests of mixed-head attention, separator selection and periodic-token retention. These substantially strengthen examination of whether separator-specific selection matters beyond generic sparse retention, supplementing v4's existing cache-size, neighboring-token, hybrid-layer and positional-shift analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained results are unchanged after matching table numbers. New Tables 9 and 15–17 add substantial comparison and ablation results: Table 15 reports strict GSM8K-CoT accuracy of 77.18 for SepLLM versus 75.06, 73.62 and 72.02 for H2O, SnapKV and PyramidKV at nearly matched KV usage. New Table 16 also contains unexplained StreamingLLM discrepancies relative to retained Table 1, including n=256 KV usage of 31.92% versus 26.00%; these do not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The encoder-based universal-approximation theorem, assumptions and proof in v4 Appendices G–H are retained in v6 Appendices J–K. The new Section 5 summarizes the existing result as Theorem 5.1 without adding mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: separator-based compression, efficient training and inference, over 50% KV reduction on GSM8K-CoT, and streaming through four million tokens. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v6 attributes the mixed-head baseline's failure to head heterogeneity, recommends including common separator types, and interprets FixLLM results as evidence for separator-specific summarization. Section 6 adds a native-sparse-attention interpretation. The earlier mechanism discussion remains in Appendix H.

D1.justification: The new experiments document head fractions and window sizes, separator subsets, and FixLLM stride and initial-token settings (Tables 9, 16–17). Existing training recipes, runtime measurements and public-code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds citations to Native Sparse Attention, Self-adjust softmax and two 2025 recommendation papers. Section 6 additionally positions SepLLM as a potential replacement for StreamingLLM as a sparse-attention baseline. The main related-work discussion is largely retained; publication updates to existing references do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: Localized copyediting and terminology changes accompany new comparison and discussion sections, an existing-theorem summary, additional appendices and updated cross-references. Most existing prose remains unchanged. The running title and publication footer are also revised.

P2.justification: v6 adds Tables 9 and 15–17, renumbers former Tables 9–13 as 10–14, and reflows appendix material. All fourteen figures retain their graphics. Captions and table labels receive limited edits within the existing two-column format.

improvement.justification: Competitive KV-cache comparisons and separator/fixed-interval controls strengthen the empirical support while preserving earlier experiments and proofs. The gain is limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 16's StreamingLLM n=256 accuracy and KV usage conflict with retained Table 1, and its n=380 flexible/strict scores are reversed. These issues weaken the precision of the new ablation, but the broader comparisons and diagnostic controls still provide a modest net improvement.
